input.description: Cupriavidus necator that fixes carbon dioxide and swims

taxon.label: Cupriavidus necator
taxon.chosen_because: most specific of the taxon words found (subclass of the others)

source.entry: scientific name read from the description

conflicts.label: fin
conflicts.note: "fin" carries no never_in_taxon axiom that reaches Cupriavidus necator. It was dropped by its in_taxon statements: the ontology asserts it only for taxa that neither contain nor are contained by Cupriavidus necator. The structure is kept out of the blueprint and reported here; nothing in the hierarchy stands for it.
conflicts.axiom: "fin" carries no never_in_taxon axiom that reaches Cupriavidus necator. It was dropped by its in_taxon statements: the ontology asserts it only for taxa that neither contain nor are contained by Cupriavidus necator.

absence.note: Structures the description asked to be absent. Each was removed from the hierarchy with everything the ontology places inside it, and every removed node is listed here.

counts_note: counts are placements in the hierarchy: a tissue or cell type that is part of several organs is counted once per organ. counts_distinct are distinct ontology terms. Use counts_distinct when saying how many tissues or cell types a blueprint has.

pruning.note: The per-parent limits below cap how many organs per system, tissues per organ and cell types per organ enter the blueprint; everything they cut is listed here with the query it came from, so a raised limit reproduces it from the cache. A structure named in the description is never cut: it is added before the limit applies and kept even where Uberon does not class it as an organ. So if the description names a structure and the blueprint lacks it, the limits are not the reason; look at reading.words_not_recognised and reading.conflicts.

genome_sketch.label: SKETCH
genome_sketch.note: Not a genome. These are marker gene products (Protein Ontology terms) that the Cell Ontology or its Provisional Cell Ontology extension records as expressed by the listed cell types (relation RO_0002292 "expresses"), reduced to the most specific term per cell. Most cell types carry no such annotation, so absence means nothing. Predicting a genome from a description is out of scope and would be labelled a sketch too.

honesty: Every node is an existing ontology term; the tool invents no names or identifiers.
Edges are Uberon/CL part_of or subClassOf statements as served by Ubergraph on the retrieval date, including inferred ones.

Taxon constraints (never_in_taxon on the term, its superclasses or its wholes; in_taxon on the term) remove structures the ontology says the taxon cannot have. For non-vertebrates, terms Uberon marks vertebrate_core are removed as well. Absence of a constraint does not mean the taxon has the structure: each organ carries taxon_evidence saying whether Uberon states it for an ancestor of the taxon or merely does not exclude it.

Organ systems and organs are limited to terms Uberon marks in its own core subsets (uberon_slim, efo_slim, vertebrate_core, major_organ, organ_slim); structures named in the description are kept regardless.
Organs are ranked major organs first, then by how many cell types the Cell Ontology records for them, which measures curation effort, not biology.
Links from a function word to a structure come either from the ontology (capable_of, reported as such) or from the hand-written lexicon (reported as curated).

A description is read at the most specific lexicon entry that matches it, longest phrase first; a shorter reading wholly inside a longer one is recorded under reading.anatomy_words_subsumed instead of being added again.

Words the lexicon does not know are listed under reading.words_not_recognised. The tool reads a word list, not English: an unrecognised word means the blueprint says nothing about whatever that word named.

Everything the per-parent limits cut is listed under "pruning", and structures named in the description are never cut. A named structure absent from the blueprint was either unrecognised or taxon-excluded, and both are reported.

A structure the description asks NOT to have is read as an absence, not as a mention: it is kept out of the blueprint and everything the ontology places inside it is removed, all of it listed under "absence". Whether the remainder is a viable animal is not checked here, and nothing in this file should be read as saying it is.
The genome sketch is marker gene products from the Cell Ontology, not a genome.
Descriptions that resolve inside the held-out clade are refused and leave no file behind; the check and its query are recorded under "holdout" for every built blueprint.
